ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r1.claim: Balad warned Quraysh that Makkah’s prosperity came through Abraham’s prayer and the House, so they must not become arrogant; Shams warns what follows if they persist.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r1.anchor: warned of their fate should they persist in their arrogance

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r4.claim: God tolerates arrogance and disorder only while expedient, then destroys those whose collective existence threatens the world; Thamūd exemplify the warning to Quraysh.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r4.anchor: When these things cross the bounds, the Almighty destroys them and cleanses His world from people whose existence becomes dangerous for it in their collective capacity

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p330/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p330/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p330/r1.claim: The Quraysh are warned that if they adopt Thamūd’s arrogant attitude, God will seize them and no one can help.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p330/r1.anchor: no one would be able to help them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r4.claim: Nations are punished collectively in this world for collective rebellion, while each person is individually judged and rewarded or punished in the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r4.anchor: In the Hereafter, each person will be held accountable in his personal capacity

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r5.claim: Historical evidence shows that a rebellious nation is given time and a clear warning, then destroyed if it persists in denial without excuse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r5.anchor: it is communicated the truth to the extent that it is left with no excuse to deny the truth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r1.claim: Cosmic and inward evidence mainly serves reflective intellectuals; historical incidents can move ordinary people who are able to learn from them, so the Qur’an uses both forms of proof.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r1.anchor: evidence from incidents and events are more effective

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r2.claim: The Qur’an mentions Thamūd alone here, although it names many nations elsewhere; its history was especially familiar to the Quraysh.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r2.anchor: has mentioned many nations to highlight this aspect

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r3.claim: Islahi quotes his mentor Imām Farāhī: Quraysh knew the Thamūd’s history, and the Qur’anic allusion was enough to evoke the whole account, including their inherited settlements and traditions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r3.anchor: has discussed their history and their resemblance

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r4.claim: The brief Qur’anic account could evoke the Thamūd’s full fate for the Quraysh because their history was familiar and often discussed among them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r4.anchor: was enough to point to their complete history

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r5.claim: A cited Arabic couplet treats Qidār as a figure overcome by time, evidence that Thamūd were known in Arab poetry.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r1.claim: Thamūd’s rebellion, leaders’ deviance, and fate were proverbial among Arabs, so the Qur’an’s short reference conveyed a full history to its first audience.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r1.anchor: so well known to the Arabs

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r2.claim: Ṭaghwā means insurgency against God’s bounds, especially rebellion after truth has become clear.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r2.anchor: It means insurgency and rebelling against the bounds and limits set by the Almighty.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r3.claim: The word connects the passage to its central theme: Thamūd denied their prophet from arrogance after truth was evident, not because it was unclear.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r3.anchor: they in fact denied him after the truth had become obvious to them merely out of their arrogance and rebelliousness.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r4.claim: After describing the failure of the one who debases himself, God names a people as an example from which others should learn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r4.anchor: ولما قال: وقد خاب من دساها، أعقبه بأهل الجنة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r5.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r5.claim: Most exegetes take the bāʾ in بطغواها as causal: Thamūd denied their prophet because of their transgression.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r5.anchor: بطغواها: الباء عند الجمهور سببية، أي كذبت ثمود نبيها بسبب طغيانها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says ṭaghwā means the punishment they denied until it came upon them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الطغوى هنا العذاب، كذبوا به حتى نزل بهم لقوله:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r7.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r7.claim: The majority read ṭaghwā with an open ṭāʾ, a verbal noun from ṭughyān with yāʾ changed to wāw to distinguish noun from adjective.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: بطغواها بفتح الطاء، وهو مصدر من الطغيان، قلبت فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r8.speaker: الحسن ومحمد بن كعب وحماد بن سلمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r8.claim: Al-Hasan, Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, and Ḥammād ibn Salama read ṭugwā with a ḍamma, a verbal noun analogous to al-rajʿā, anomalous for this root.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p489#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ومحمد بن كعب وحماد بن سلمة: بضم الطاء، وهو مصدر كالرجعى،

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r9.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3437/r9.claim: Mujahid says Thamud denied through their transgression, meaning their disobedience.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r11.claim: The oath answer is that God will devastate Mecca for rejecting the Messenger, as He devastated Thamud for rejecting Salih; قد أفلح is a digression continuing the preceding point, not the oath answer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r11.anchor: على أهل مكة لتكذيبهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

STUDYQURAN:91:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:91:intro/r3.claim: The final verses use Thamūd as an example of those destroyed for rejecting and disobeying messengers; its appearance in early and later surahs indicates the story was well known to Arabs.
STUDYQURAN:91:intro/r3.anchor: The last five verses focus on the story of the northern Arabian tribe Thamūd as an example of what befalls those who reject God’s messengers

TABRISI:91:1-15#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:1-15#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:91:1-15#2/r3.claim: Thamud denied because of rebellion and disobedience; their tyranny drove them to denial.
TABRISI:91:1-15#2/r3.anchor: أي بطغيانها ومعصيتها عن مجاهد وابن زيد يعني أن الطغيان حملهم على التكذيب

TABRISI:91:1-15#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:1-15#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:91:1-15#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, ṭaghwā means the punishment they denied, connected with the punishment called al-ṭāghiyah.
TABRISI:91:1-15#2/r4.anchor: إن الطغوى اسم العذاب الذي نزل بهم فالمعنى كذبت ثمود بعذابها عن ابن عباس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r5.claim: This contrast prepares the lesson of Thamūd: their punishment followed from corrupting their souls through arrogance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p370/r5.anchor: وهذه الجملة توطئة لجملة : كذبت ثمود بطغواها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r1.claim: If success and failure answer the oath, Thamūd's denial is evidence for the failure of those who corrupt their souls.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r1.anchor: في موقع الدليل لمضمون جملة { وقد خاب من دساها }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r4.claim: If the success statement is parenthetical, the story's consequence of Thamūd's destruction answers the oath; its lām is omitted to shorten an already long oath, as in Sūrat al-Burūj.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r4.anchor: ولام الجواب محذوف تخفيفا لاستطالة القسم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r5.claim: The oath indirectly threatens the arrogant Quraysh, who resemble Thamūd in knowingly rejecting the Messenger; God swears they will suffer a like punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r5.anchor: التعريض بتهديد المشركين الذين كذبوا الرسول طغيانا هم يعلمونه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r6.claim: The Meccans had experienced the sword's punishment at the hands of enemies after persecuting and expelling the Prophet, a particularly bitter chastisement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r6.anchor: ولقد أصاب المشركين عذاب السيف بأيدي الذين عادوهم وآذوهم وأخرجوهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r1.claim: The object of 'denied' is omitted but supplied from the next clause: Thamūd denied their Messenger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r1.anchor: فمفعول { كذبت } محذوف لدلالة قوله بعده : { فقال لهم رسول الله }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r2.claim: The bāʾ in biṭaghwā expresses cause: extreme arrogance caused them to deny the Messenger; this parallels Quraysh's pride at following someone they thought socially inferior.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r3.claim: The time of the worst arrogance was when they chose their most wicked man to hamstring the she-camel, the climax of their defiance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r3.anchor: لأن وقت انبعاث أشقاها لعقر الناقة هو الوقت الذي بدت فيه شدة طغواها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r7.claim: The first fa sequences the denial and Salih's challenge: he showed the she-camel as a sign and warned them not to harm it or deprive it of its turn to drink.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r7.anchor: فتحداهم بآية الناقة وحذرهم من التعرض لها بسوء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r1.claim: Alternatively, the fa merely introduces details after a general statement, as in other Quranic examples; Thamūd denied through arrogance when their most wicked man rose, with the warning and hamstringing then elaborating the episode.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الفاء للترتيب الذكري المجرد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r2.claim: Plural pronouns are used because Thamūd are a people collectively, although the earlier reference treats Thamūd grammatically as a tribe name.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r2.anchor: وأعيدت عليهم ضمائر الجمع باعتبار أنهم جمع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r12.claim: After the warning about a ruined soul, God recalls a people whose fate supplies a lesson against such conduct.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r12.anchor: ولما ذكر تعالى خيبة من دسى نفسه، ذكر فرقة فعلت ذلك يعتبر بهم وينتهى عن مثل فعلهم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r13.speaker: الحسن وحماد بن سليمان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r13.claim: They read ṭughwāhā with ḍamma on ṭāʾ, using a verbal-noun pattern like ʿuqbā and rujʿā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r13.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وحماد بن سليمان «بطغواها» بضم الطاء مصدر كالعقبى والرجعى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas says ṭaghwā is the punishment they denied until it came upon them, supported by the account of Thamud's destruction elsewhere.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r14.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: «الطغوى» هنا العذاب كذبوا به حتى نزل بهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r15.speaker: جمهور المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r15.claim: Most interpreters take the bāʾ causally: Thamud denied their prophet because of rebellion and unbelief.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r15.anchor: وقال جمهور المتأولين الباء سببية، والمعنى كذبت ثمود بنبيها بسبب طغيانها وكفرها،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p142/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p142/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p142/r1.claim: Thamūd denied its messenger because of its tyranny; the tyranny drove it to denial, and ṭaghwā is a verbal noun like ṭughyān, chosen to match the verse endings. Another view says they denied the punishment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p142/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى كذبت ثمود بطغواها أي كذبت رسولها بطغيانها

IBNKATHIR:91:11/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:11/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:91:11/r1.claim: Thamud denied its messenger because of its transgression and aggression, which caused denial of the guidance and certainty he brought to take hold in their hearts.
IBNKATHIR:91:11/r1.anchor: يخبر تعالى عن ثمود أنهم كذبوا رسولهم ،   بسبب ما كانوا عليه من الطغيان والبغي .

IBNKATHIR:91:11/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:11/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNKATHIR:91:11/r2.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb interprets bi-ṭaghwāhā as “all of them together.”
IBNKATHIR:91:11/r2.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب : { بِطَغْوَاهَا } أي : بأجمعها .

IBNKATHIR:91:11/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:11/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:91:11/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers the transgression interpretation, also reported from Mujahid, Qatada, and others.
IBNKATHIR:91:11/r3.anchor: والأول أولى ،   قاله مجاهد وقتادة وغيرهما .

FARRA:v3p267/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p267/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p267/r1.claim: The rare form ṭaghwāh means ṭughyānihā, “its rebellion”; it was chosen to fit the verse endings.
FARRA:v3p267/r1.anchor: بطغواها (11) أراد بطغيانها إلا أن الطغوى أشكل برءوس الآيات فاختير لذلك.

FARRA:v3p267/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p267/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p267/r2.claim: Daʿwāhum can mean their supplication, as in the cited verses about their final prayer and their prayer in Paradise.
FARRA:v3p267/r2.anchor: «وآخر دعواهم أن الحمد لله .» ومعناه آخر دعائهم، وكذلك «دعواهم فيها سبحانك اللهم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p530#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p530#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p530#3/r1.claim: Thamūd denied their messenger because of their rebellion.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p530#3/r1.anchor: {كذبت ثمود بطغواها} أي كذبت الرسول إليها بطغيانها.

JISHUMI:v10p7434/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7434/r2.speaker: الحسن وحماد بن سلمة
JISHUMI:v10p7434/r2.claim: They read طغواها with ḍamma on ṭā; the common reading has fatḥa, and both are dialect forms.
JISHUMI:v10p7434/r2.anchor: وعن الحسن وحماد بن سلمة بضم الطاء، وهما لغتان

JISHUMI:v10p7434/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7434/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7434/r4.claim: Ṭaghwā means exceeding limits in corruption and disobedience; it may be a faʿlā form from ṭāghiya, like taqwā.
JISHUMI:v10p7434/r4.anchor: الطغوى: مجاوزة الحد في الفساد والعصيان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r1.claim: The preposition in bithaghwaha works like the ba in “wrote with a pen”; the noun form changes weak y to waw unlike its adjective, meaning they denied because of rebellion.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r1.anchor: الباء في { بطغواها } مثلها في : كتبت بالقلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, Thamud denied the punishment promised for its overwhelming rebellion, as in 69:5.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : كذبت بما أوعدت به من عذابها ذي الطغوى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r3.claim: Hasan reads ṭaghwāhā with a damma, like other verbal nouns.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن : ( بطغواها ) بضم الطاء كالحسنى والرجعى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p765/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p765/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p765/r1.claim: A report says reciting the Sun sura is like giving charity on everything illuminated by the sun and moon.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p765/r1.anchor: من قرأ سورة الشمس ، فكأنما تصدق بكل شيء طلعت عليه الشمس والقمر

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r1.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r1.claim: They interpret ṭaghwāhā as Thamud's tyranny and disobedience.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r2.claim: He interprets the phrase as referring to all of Thamud collectively.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r3.claim: He says ṭaghwāhā was the name of the punishment that struck Thamud.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r3.anchor: بعذابها , قاله ابن عباس . قالوا كان اسم العذاب

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r4.claim: Damdama may mean He became angry with them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r5.claim: Damdama may mean He enclosed or encompassed them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r6.claim: Damdama may mean He destroyed them; the word is of Abyssinian origin adopted into Arabic.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r6.anchor: وهو مثل دمدم , كلمة بالحبشية نطقت بها العرب

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r7.speaker: السدي ويحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r7.claim: They interpret fa-sawwāhā as making them equal in destruction.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r8.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r8.claim: He interprets it as leveling them with the earth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r8.anchor: فسوى بهم الأرض , ذكره ابن شجرة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r9.claim: A further possibility is that God leveled later nations after them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r10.claim: He says God does not fear the consequence of destroying them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r10.anchor: ما صنع بهم من الهلاك , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r11.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r11.claim: He says the person who hamstrung the she-camel does not fear the consequence of the deed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r11.anchor: ما صنع من عقرها , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r12.claim: A further possibility is that Salih did not fear the consequence because he had warned them and God rescued him when they were destroyed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p285/r12.anchor: ولا يخاف صالح عقبى عقرها , لأنه قد أنذرهم

MUJAHID:v2p763#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p763#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p763#3/r1.claim: Mujahid says Thamud denied the truth through their disobedience.
MUJAHID:v2p763#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ بطغواها ﴾ قال يعني بمعصيتها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#5/r1.claim: Thamud denied because of their transgression, which drove them to denial.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#5/r1.anchor: بطغيانها إذا لحامل لهم على التكذيب طغيانهم

QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari infers that God will destroy Meccans for denying Muhammad as He destroyed Thamud for denying Salih; verses 9–10 are an aside, not the oath’s answer.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r3.anchor: الزمخشري: تقديره ليدمدمن الله عليهم أي على أهل مكة، لتكذيبهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، كما دمدم على ثمود لأنهم كذبوا صالحا

QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r1.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r1.claim: They say Thamud denied because of transgression, exceeding bounds in disobedience.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r1.anchor: أي بطغيانها، وهو خروجها عن الحد في العصيان قاله مجاهد وقتادة وغيرهما

QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says taghwa means the punishment promised to Thamud, named for overpowering them.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس «بطغواها» أي بعذابها الذي وعدت به

QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Kab takes the word to refer to their collective transgression.

QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r4.claim: It may be an infinitive form chosen to fit the verse endings.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو مصدر، وخرج على هذا المخرج، لأنه أشكل برؤوس الآي

QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r5.claim: The underlying form may be taghyaha, with final yāʾ changed to wāw in the noun to distinguish it from an adjective.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r5.anchor: وقيل: الأصل بطغياها، إلا أن «فعلى» إذا كانت من ذوات الياء

QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r6.claim: The common reading has fatḥa on ṭāʾ; al-Hasan, al-Jahdari, and Hammad ibn Salama read ḍamma as an infinitive or dialect variant.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:11-12/r6.anchor: وقراءة العامة بفتح الطاء. وقرأ الحسن والجحدري وحماد بن سلمة بضم الطاء على أنه مصدر كالرجعى والحسنى

NAHHAS:v5p237/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p237/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p237/r1.claim: Al-ṭaghwā and al-ṭughyān are synonymous; the report from Ibn ʿAbbās instead reads it as their punishment, a noun for torment, with an omitted iḍāfah understood.
NAHHAS:v5p237/r1.anchor: الطغوى الطغيان واحد إلا أن عطاء الخراساني روى عن ابن عباس قال بطغواها بعذابها

NAHHAS:v5p237/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p237/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p237/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī, interprets bi-ṭaghwāhā as their punishment.
NAHHAS:v5p237/r2.anchor: عطاء الخراساني روى عن ابن عباس قال بطغواها بعذابها

NAHHAS:v5p237/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p237/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p237/r3.claim: That reading is grammatical with an omitted phrase, bi-ʿadhābi ṭaghwāhā, as in asking a town while meaning its people.
NAHHAS:v5p237/r3.anchor: وهذا يصح على حذف أي بعذاب طغواها مثل وسئل القرية

QUTB-ZILAL:91:11/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:91:11/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:91:11/r1.claim: Thamud exemplifies failure: tyranny hid the people from guidance and defiled them, bringing divine anger and destruction; Qutb directs readers to fuller earlier accounts, especially Sura al-Fajr.
QUTB-ZILAL:91:11/r1.anchor: وقد وردت قصة ثمود ونبيها صالح - عليه السلام - في مواضع شتى من القرآن

QUTB-ZILAL:91:11/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:91:11/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:91:11/r2.claim: Here Qutb says Thamud denied its prophet because of its transgression; tyranny itself was the cause of denial.
QUTB-ZILAL:91:11/r2.anchor: فكان الطغيان وحده هو سبب التكذيب

RAZI-FULL:v31p176#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p176#2/r1.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v31p176#2/r1.claim: Al-Farra says ṭughyān and ṭugwā are verbal nouns; ṭugwā fits the verse endings, like daʿwā from daʿā.

RAZI-FULL:v31p176#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p176#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p176#2/r2.claim: The common interpretation is that Thamud's rebelliousness drove them to deny the messenger.

RAZI-FULL:v31p176#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p176#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p176#2/r3.claim: Another view takes ṭugwā as the punishment they denied when they disbelieved the messenger's warning.
RAZI-FULL:v31p176#2/r3.anchor: أن الطغوى اسم لعذابهم الذي أهلكوا به

RAZI-FULL:v31p176#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p176#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p176#2/r4.claim: Razi says the punishment reading is plausible because ṭughyān means exceeding bounds; the unusual cry could be called ṭugwā, as al-Hāqqa names their punishment with related terms.
RAZI-FULL:v31p176#2/r4.anchor: لأن معنى الطغيان في اللغة مجاوزة القدر المعتاد

SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī begins with an instrumental, metaphorical bāʾ: Thamūd committed denial by its own overweening transgression.
SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r1.anchor: أحدها: أنها للاستعانة مجازا، كقوله: " كتبت بالقلم " وبه بدأ الزمخشري

SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r2.claim: A second analysis makes bāʾ causative: they denied what they were threatened with, the punishment of the transgressing blast, as in 69:5.
SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r2.anchor: الثاني: أنها للتعدية، أي: كذبت بما أوعدت به من عذابها ذي الطغيان

SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r3.claim: A third analysis makes bāʾ causal: Thamūd denied because of its transgression.
SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r3.anchor: والثالث: أنها للسببية، أي: بسبب طغيانها

SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r4.claim: The common fatḥ reading ṭaghwāhā is a verbal noun meaning tyranny; yā is changed to wāw in the noun to distinguish it from the adjective.
SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r4.anchor: وقرأ العامة " طغواها " بفتح الطاء وهو مصدر بمعنى الطغيان، وإنما قلبت الياء واوا فرقا بين الاسم والصفة

SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r5.speaker: الحسن، محمد بن كعب، حماد
SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, and Ḥammād read with ḍamma on ṭāʾ; this too is a verbal noun but is irregular if the verb is ṭaghaytu.
SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r5.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ومحمد بن كعب وحماد بضم الطاء، وهو أيضا مصدر كالرجعى والحسنى، إلا أن هذا شاذ

SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r6.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ says the wāw is original for speakers who use the verb ṭaghawtu rather than ṭaghaytu.
SAMIN-DURR:91:11/r6.anchor: فالواو أصل عنده، قاله ابو البقاء، وقد تقدم الكلام على اللغتين في البقرة والله الحمد.

STUDYQURAN:91:11/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:11/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:91:11/r1.claim: Thamūd exemplifies a people who obscure the soul through disobedience; the northern Arabian tribe rejected the Prophet Ṣāliḥ.
STUDYQURAN:91:11/r1.anchor: The tribe of Thamūd is cited as an example of those who “obscure” the soul through disobedience.

TAB-FULL:v24p446/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p446/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p446/r1.claim: Ṭabarī interprets ṭughwā as the punishment promised by Ṣāliḥ, which overwhelmed Thamūd, and links it to the punishment called al-ṭāghiya.
TAB-FULL:v24p446/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قول الله: {كذبت ثمود بطغواها} [الشمس: 11] قال: اسم العذاب الذي جاءها، الطغوى، فقال: كذبت ثمود بعذابها

TAB-FULL:v24p446/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p446/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p446/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says al-ṭughwā was the name of Thamūd's punishment, so they denied the punishment itself.
TAB-FULL:v24p446/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قول الله: {كذبت ثمود بطغواها} [الشمس: 11] قال: اسم العذاب الذي جاءها، الطغوى

TAB-FULL:v24p446/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p446/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p446/r3.claim: Qatāda interprets the phrase as denial through tyrannical transgression.
TAB-FULL:v24p446/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {كذبت ثمود بطغواها} [الشمس: 11] أي: بالطغيان

TAB-FULL:v24p446/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p446/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p446/r4.claim: Mujāhid says they denied because of their disobedience to God.
TAB-FULL:v24p446/r4.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، {كذبت ثمود بطغواها} [الشمس: 11] قال: معصيتها

TAB-FULL:v24p446/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p446/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p446/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd combines both ideas, interpreting ṭughwā as their transgression and disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v24p446/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {كذبت ثمود بطغواها} [الشمس: 11] قال: بطغيانهم وبمعصيتهم

TAB-FULL:v24p446/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p446/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v24p446/r6.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb says they denied by all of their misdeeds taken together.
TAB-FULL:v24p446/r6.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب، أنه قال: {كذبت ثمود بطغواها} [الشمس: 11] قال: بأجمعها

TAB-FULL:v24p446/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p446/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p446/r7.claim: Ṭughwā and ṭughyān are equivalent verbal nouns; ṭughwā suits this sūra's rhyme, like the wording in 10:10.
TAB-FULL:v24p446/r7.anchor: وقيل {طغواها} بمعنى: طغيانهم، وهما مصدران للتوفيق بين رءوس الآي

TABATABAI:91:11-15/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:91:11-15/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:91:11-15/r2.claim: Thamūd’s denial was caused by its rebellion; their story through the end of the sūra demonstrates the preceding contrast between purification and corruption.
TABATABAI:91:11-15/r2.anchor: الطغوى مصدر كالطغيان، والباء للسببية. والآية وما يتلوها إلى آخر السورة استشهاد وتقرير لما تقدم

ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r6.claim: Ṭaghwā means tyranny and derives from ṭughyān; in a faʿlā noun from a root with yāʾ, yāʾ becomes wāw to distinguish noun from adjective, as in taqwā and khazyā.
ZAJJAJ:v5p332/r6.anchor:
أي بطغيانها، وأصل (طغواها) طغيها وفعلى إذا كانت من ذوات الياء
أبدلت في الاسم واوا

TABRISI:91:14/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:14/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:91:14/r12.claim: Inbaʿatha means to be roused or sent forth; baʿatha is what causes that response.
TABRISI:91:14/r12.anchor: وبعث مطاوع انبعث يقال بعثته على الأمر فانبعث له

THALABI:v10p214/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p214/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p214/r1.claim: Thamud denied because of their tyranny and hostility.

THALABI:v10p214/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p214/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p214/r2.claim: Via ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī, he says al-ṭaghwā is the name of the punishment, so the phrase means they denied their punishment.
THALABI:v10p214/r2.anchor: وروى عطاء الخراساني عن ابن عباس قال: اسم العذاب الذي جاءهم الطغوى

THALABI:v10p214/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p214/r3.speaker: الحسن وحماد بن سلمة
THALABI:v10p214/r3.claim: They read ṭaghwā with ḍamma, while the common reading has fatḥa; both are dialect forms like fatwā and fitwā.
THALABI:v10p214/r3.anchor: وقرأه العامة بفتح الطاء، وقرأ الحسن وحماد بن سلمة بطغواها بضم الطاء

ASAD-NOTES:91:11#n7/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:91:11#n7/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:91:11#n7/r1.claim: Asad points to 7:73–79 and its notes for Thamud's story, used here to illustrate humanity's potential wickedness.
ASAD-NOTES:91:11#n7/r1.anchor: given here as an illustration of man's potential wickedness

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r1.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭughyā and al-ṭughwān are dialectal verbal nouns for transgression; the verbs are ṭaghaytu and ṭaghawtu, and al-ṭughwā is the noun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r1.anchor: الطغيان و [الطغوان] (¬3) لغة فيه، والفعل طغيت، وطغوت (¬4) والاسم: الطغوى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r2.claim: The intended meaning is their transgression; both forms are verbal nouns, but al-ṭughwā better matches the verse endings, like al-daʿwā from supplication.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r2.anchor: وهما مصدران إلا أن الطغوى أشكل برؤوس الآيات فاختير لذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r3.claim: He derives ṭughwā from ṭughyā; a yāʾ in this faʿlā noun changes to wāw to distinguish noun from adjective, as in taqwā and daʿwā.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: أصل طغواها طغياها، وفعلى إذا كانت من ذوات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r4.claim: Thamud's transgression impelled them to deny their prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r4.anchor: قال المفسرون: كذبت ثمود بنبيهم بطغيانهم، أي الطغيان حملهم على التكذيب به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r5.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī's report, al-ṭughyā names the punishment that destroyed Thamud.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن الطغوى اسم لعذابهم الذي أهلكوا به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r6.claim: The word can refer to their punishment: they denied the warning of punishment, and an extraordinary blast could be called transgression because it exceeded the usual limit.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p64#2/r6.anchor: والمعنى: كذبت بعذابها، أي لم يصدقوا رسولهم فيما أنذرهم به من العذاب

WAHIDI-QT:91:11/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:91:11/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:91:11/r1.claim: Thamud denied the messengers through their transgression.
WAHIDI-QT:91:11/r1.anchor: { كذبت ثمود بطغواها } بطغيانها كذبت الرسل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r3.claim: Thamud denied the messengers through their transgression.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r3.anchor: كذبت ثمود بطغواها } بطغيانها كذبت الرسل.

ELMALILI:91:11-15/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r1.claim: Thamud were an ancient Arabian people whose destruction and story remained famous; God sent Salih, and when they demanded a sign he showed them the miraculous she-camel with a warning not to harm it.
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r1.anchor: Allah teâlâ onlara peygamber olarak Sâlih aleyhisselâm’ı ba‘s buyurmuş

ELMALILI:91:11-15/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r2.claim: The camel's appointed alternating drinking day was part of the sign; it was to graze freely, and harming it would bring painful punishment.
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r2.anchor: onun suvarılmasına münâvebe suretiyle bir gün tahsis olunmuş

ELMALILI:91:11-15/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r3.claim: They rejected both the miracle and the truthful warning; denying a true report is falsehood and sin, while denying a prophet's report is disbelief in the God who sent him.
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r3.anchor: bir peygamberin ihbârını tekzib ise onu gönderen Allah’a küfürdür.

ELMALILI:91:11-15/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r4.claim: Taghwa means rebellion; relying on their strength as rock-cutters, Thamud denied their prophet in arrogance.

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r1.claim: Q 91, 89, and 85 contain three Group II allusions to Thamud, Ad, and Pharaoh; alongside Q 105, they are the earliest narrative Quranic texts and the nucleus of later punishment legends.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Der Abschnitt gehört zu den insgesamt drei Passagen in Gruppe II der frühmekkanischen Suren, in denen Anspielungen auf die Ṯamūd, die ʿĀd und auf Pharao begegnen

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r2.claim: The fullest other early-Makkan Thamud account is later Q 54:23–31; shorter allusions also occur in 89, 69, and 51, while Q 85 and 89 connect the story to Pharaoh and Ad.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Eine relativ ausführliche Darstellung der Ṯamūd-Legende findet sich in frühmekkanischer Zeit nur noch in der sicherlich später als Q 91 anzusetzenden Passage 54:23–31

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r3.claim: Umayya b. Abi al-Salt’s likely authentic poem lacks a divine warner and explicit command; the camel’s foal’s curse triggers destruction, and its named culprit Aḥmar is elsewhere associated with Ad, perhaps showing tribal names or traditions overlapped.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Es fehlt die Figur eines göttlich gesandten Warners, dessen expliziten Anweisungen die Ṯamūd zuwider handeln, und ihre Vernichtung wird durch einen Fluch ausgelöst

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11:anmerkung/r1.claim: Unlike 95:7 and 82:9, bi-ṭaġwāhā gives the cause of Thamud’s denial, not what they denied: they denied out of rebelliousness.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11:anmerkung/r1.anchor: gibt die Präpositionalgruppe bi-ṭaġwāhā im vorliegenden Vers jedoch nicht den Gegenstand des Leugnens an, sondern seine Ursache

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11:anmerkung/r2.speaker: Müller
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11:anmerkung/r2.claim: Müller reads ṭaġwā as a rhyme-driven variant of ṭuġyān; the author notes that all Quranic ṭuġyān occurrences postdate this sura.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Müller 1969, 64–68, will ṭaġwā als reimbedingte Variante für das gebräuchlichere ṭuġyān verstehen

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11:anmerkung/r3.claim: The root ṭ-ġ-w/y also appears with Thamud at 69:5, but there aṭ-ṭāġiya is the punishment that overtakes them, unlike ṭaġwā here, their disobedience.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11:anmerkung/r3.anchor: aṭ-ṭāġiya bezeichnet dort das die Ṯamūd „überkommende“ Strafgericht

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r1.claim: This is the oldest genuine Quranic punishment legend: it recasts the likely pre-Islamic Thamud story as an example of the choice between good and evil and may mirror the Quranic preacher’s rejection by hearers.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r1.anchor: Die vorliegende Sure funktionalisiert die sicherlich bereits in vorkoranischer Zeit bekannte Ṯamūd-Legende als historisches Exempel für die Konsequenzen der zuvor formulierten Alternative von Gut und Böse

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r2.claim: Compared with Umayya’s poem, the Quran adds a divine messenger and an explicit command to spare the camel; the pre-Islamic offense was cultic disrespect toward a consecrated camel, so the Quran theologically reconfigures the inherited story.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r2.anchor: Das Vergehen der Ṯamūd wird bei Umayya als ein Kultfrevel geschildert, als Mißachtung der Unverletzlichkeit eines geweihten Kamels, nicht als Übertretung eines – durch einen prophetischen Boten überbrachten – göttlichen Verbots.

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r4.claim: The passage foregrounds ethical judgment rather than description: it calls Thamud deniers and rebels in verse 11, then repeats kadhdhaba in verse 14 to make rejection of the messenger the immediate cause of destruction; the term may reflect Syriac kaddeb.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r4.anchor: Ein zweites Mal erscheint das Verb kaḏḏaba – das offenbar bereits terminologischen Status hat und wohl mit syr. kaddeb in Verbindung zu bringen ist

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r5.claim: The Quran omits Umayya’s aftermath in which a lame servant survives, reports the event, and dies, since that addition does not serve the general lesson.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r5.anchor: Die theologische Zuspitzung der koranischen Version wird überdies daran sichtbar, dass hier das bei Umayya erzählte Nachspiel

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:11/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:11/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:11/r1.claim: The account of Thamud exemplifies a community's wrong choice after humans were given the ability to choose good or evil; its destruction is a warning, as in the accounts in al-A'raf and Hud.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:11/r1.anchor: Semûd kavminin yanlış seçimi ve bu yüzden başlarına gelen büyük felâket

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p372#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p372#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p372#2/r1.claim: كذبت ثمود is read with assimilation or clear articulation; Ibn Khālawayh points back to earlier explanations of the two forms.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p372#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ كذبت ثمود ﴾ يقرأ بالادغام والاظهار وقد ذكرت علل ذلك فيما مضى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r1.claim: The Thamūd account resumes the argument by confirming that whoever corrupts the soul fails.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r1.anchor: استئناف وارد لتقرير مضمون قوله تعالى وقد خاب من دساها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats the purification statements as a parenthesis and makes the oath's omitted answer a threat to destroy Meccan disbelievers as Thamūd were destroyed for rejecting Ṣāliḥ.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r2.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري قوله تعالى قد أفلح الخ تابعا لقوله تعالى فألهمها الخ على سبيل الأستطراد وأبى أن يكون جواب القسم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r3.claim: Alusi objects that omitting the laam is far more common and less cumbersome than omitting an entire clause; purification is itself a central aim, not merely a practical-intellect concern or disposable preliminary.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144/r3.anchor: وتعقب بأن حذف اللام كثير لاسيما مع الطول وهو أسهل من حذف الجملة بتمامها وقد ذكره في قد أفلح المؤمنون

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r7.claim: Ṭaghwā is a verbal noun for transgression and exceeding the limit in disobedience. Al-Zamakhsharī explains why the noun shifts final ي to و while the corresponding adjective does not; al-Rāghib's evidence suggests the verb may itself be from و.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r7.anchor: والطغوى مصدر من الطغيان بمعنى تجاوز الحد في العصيان فصلوا بين الاسم والصفة في فعلى من بنات الياء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r8.claim: Most take the preposition as causal, while al-Zamakhsharī takes it instrumentally; another reading makes it complement the denial, referring to the excessively severe promised punishment without an omitted possessive.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r8.anchor: والباء عند الجمهور للسببية أي فعلت التكذيب بسبب طغيانها كما تقول ظلمني الخبيث بجرائته على الله تعالى وجعلها الزمخشري للأستعانة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, and Ḥammād ibn Salama read طغواها with ḍamma; it remains a verbal noun, though one account calls its form irregular.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p144#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ومحمد بن كعب وحماد بن سلمة طغواها بضم الطاء وهو مصدر أيضا كالرجعي والحسني

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r6.claim: Thamud’s rebellion and aggression drove them to deny the truth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p439#2/r6.anchor: بطغيانها وعدوانها، أي الطغيان حملهم على التكذيب

BAYDAWI-FULL:91:9-11/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:9-11/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:9-11/r4.claim: Thamūd denied because of its tyranny, or because it rejected the promised punishment described by طغوى; the form derives from طغياها, with a spelling distinction between noun and adjective.
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:9-11/r4.anchor: بسبب طغيانها، أو بما أوعدت به من عذابها ذي الطغوى

BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r7.claim: A report says reciting al-Shams is like giving charity over everything illuminated by the sun and moon.
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r7.anchor: من قرأ سورة والشمس فكأنما تصدق بكل شيء طلعت عليه الشمس والقمر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r9.claim: Thamūd's denial is described in the feminine because its effect was weak: listeners could plainly see its injustice and ugliness.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r10.claim: Thamūd are singled out because their signs were exceptionally clear, their remains and stories were known to Arabs, and their case points to Resurrection.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r11.claim: Ṭaghwā may mean their excessive tyranny that caused denial, or the imminent punishment by which they perished; the wāw form is preferred for its force.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p441/r11.anchor: كما ان اللئام ينزلون بطون الأودية ومقاطعها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r1.claim: The feminine verb for Thamūd's denial signals its weak effect, since the injustice and ugliness of their rejection were obvious.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r1.anchor: أنث فعلهم لضعف أثر تكذيبهم لأن كل سامع له يعرف ظلمهم فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r2.claim: Their denial arose from ṭughyān, meaning excess beyond bounds, extreme disbelief, sin, and injustice, or from the punishment that overtook them.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r2.anchor: وهو مجاوزة القدر وارتفاعه والغلو في الكفر والإسراف في المعاصي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r3.claim: The form ṭaghwā is preferred over the yāʾ form for the strength of wāw and marks the extreme degree of their denial.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r3.anchor: واختير التعبير به دون اليائي لقوة الواو

DURR-FULL:v8p528/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r7.claim: He says purification means improving the soul, concealment means leading it astray, Thamud denied through disobedience, and God does not fear their aftermath.
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r7.anchor: قال: عرفها شقاءها {قد أفلح من زكاها} قال: أصلحها {وقد خاب من دساها} قال: أغواها

DURR-FULL:v8p529/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p529/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p529/r8.claim: Thamud denied because of transgression, and their most wretched man was Uḥaymir Thamud.
DURR-FULL:v8p529/r8.anchor: قال: بالطغيان {إذ انبعث أشقاها} قال: أحيمر ثمود

DURR-FULL:v8p531/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p531/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p531/r3.claim: He says ‘ṭaghwā’ names the punishment that came upon Thamud, so they denied their punishment.
DURR-FULL:v8p531/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {كذبت ثمود بطغواها} قال: اسم العذاب الذي جاءها الطغوى

TAB:91:11/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:11/r1.speaker: author
TAB:91:11/r1.claim: Thamud denied the punishment promised by Salih; the punishment overwhelmed them, as the Qur’an also says they were destroyed by the overpowering calamity.
TAB:91:11/r1.anchor: كذّبت ثمود بطغيانها ، يعني : بعذابها الذي وعدهموه صالح عليه السلام ، فكان ذلك العذاب طاغيا طغى عليهم ، كما قال جلّ ثناؤه : فأمّا ثمود فأُهْلِكُوا بالطّاغيَة

TAB:91:11/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:11/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:91:11/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says al-ṭaghwā was the name of the punishment that came upon them, so they denied their punishment.
TAB:91:11/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قول الله : كذّبت ثمود بطَغْوَاها قال : اسم العذاب الذي جاءها ، الطّغْوَى ، فقال : كذّبت ثمود بعذابها

TAB:91:11/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:11/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB:91:11/r3.claim: Qatada glosses the phrase as denial through transgression.
TAB:91:11/r3.anchor: عن قتادة كَذّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بطَغْوَاها : أي بالطغيان

TAB:91:11/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:11/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:91:11/r4.claim: Mujahid interprets al-ṭaghwā as their disobedience.
TAB:91:11/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد كَذّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِطَغْوَاها قال : معصيتها

TAB:91:11/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:11/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:91:11/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses the phrase as their transgression and disobedience.
TAB:91:11/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد ، في قوله : كَذّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بطَغْوَاها قال : بطغيانهم وبمعصيتهم

TAB:91:11/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:11/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب
TAB:91:11/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says the phrase encompasses all the reported meanings.
TAB:91:11/r6.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب ، أنه قال : كَذّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بطَغْوَاها قال : بأجمعها

TAB:91:11/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:11/r7.speaker: author
TAB:91:11/r7.claim: Ṭaghwā and ṭughyān are both verbal nouns; the form ṭaghwā suits the rhyme of the sūra’s verse endings, like ākhiru daʿwāhum.
TAB:91:11/r7.anchor: وقيل طَغْوَاها بمعنى : طغيانهم ، وهما مصدران ، للتوفيق بين رؤوس الاَي ، إذ كانت الّطْغَوى أشبه بسائر رؤوس الاَيات في هذه السورة

ABUHAYYAN:91:11/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:11/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:91:11/r1.claim: After the fate of the one who corrupts his soul, Thamūd is recalled as a people whose fate serves as warning.
ABUHAYYAN:91:11/r1.anchor: ولما ذكر تعالى خيبة من دسى نفسه ، ذكر فرقة فعلت ذلك ليعتبر بهم

ABUHAYYAN:91:11/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:11/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:91:11/r2.claim: The majority take the bāʾ as causal: Thamūd denied its prophet because of its transgression.
ABUHAYYAN:91:11/r2.anchor: { بطغواها } : الباء عند الجمهور سببية ، أي كذبت ثمود نبيها بسبب طغيانها .

ABUHAYYAN:91:11/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:11/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN:91:11/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says ṭaghwā here means the punishment they denied until it came upon them.
ABUHAYYAN:91:11/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : الطغوى هنا العذاب ، كذبوا به حتى نزل بهم لقوله : { فأما ثمود فأهلكوا بالطاغية }

ABUHAYYAN:91:11/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:11/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:91:11/r4.claim: The majority read ṭaghwā with fatḥa on ṭāʾ; it is a verbal noun from ṭughyān, with yāʾ changed to wāw to distinguish the noun from an adjective.
ABUHAYYAN:91:11/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { بطغواها } بفتح الطاء ، وهو مصدر من الطغيان ، قلبت فيه الياء واواً فصلاً بين الاسم وبين الصفة

ABUHAYYAN:91:11/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:11/r5.speaker: الحسن ومحمد بن كعب وحماد بن سلمة
ABUHAYYAN:91:11/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, and Ḥammād ibn Salama read with ḍamma on ṭāʾ, as a verbal noun like al-rajʿā; the expected yāʾ form is anomalous here.
ABUHAYYAN:91:11/r5.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ومحمد بن كعب وحماد بن سلمة : بضم الطاء ، وهو مصدر كالرجعى ، وكان قياسها الطغيا بالياء كالسقيا

ALUSI:91:11/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:11/r1.claim: The report that Thamūd denied is a fresh sentence reinforcing the failure of the soul that was corrupted in 91:10.
ALUSI:91:11/r1.anchor: استئناف وارد لتقرير مضمون قوله تعالى

ALUSI:91:11/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI:91:11/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī makes ‘successful is whoever purified it’ parenthetical after the inspiration clause, not the oath’s answer; he infers an omitted answer that God will destroy Meccan unbelievers for rejecting the Messenger as He destroyed Thamūd for rejecting Ṣāliḥ.
ALUSI:91:11/r2.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري قوله تعالى : { قَدْ أَفْلَحَ } الخ تابعاً لقوله تعالى : { فَأَلْهَمَهَا } الخ

ALUSI:91:11/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:11/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the objection that this requires omitting the oath’s lām and improperly emphasizing practical purification over the higher goal of certain belief.
ALUSI:91:11/r3.anchor: فقيل إن ذلك لما يلزم من حذف اللام وأنه لا يليق بالنظم المعجز أن يجعل أدنى الكمالين

ALUSI:91:11/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:11/r4.claim: He replies that deleting the lām is common, especially after a long phrase, and is easier than deleting an entire sentence; al-Zamakhsharī himself accepts an omitted oath answer at 23:1.
ALUSI:91:11/r4.anchor: وقد ذكره في { قد أفلح المؤمنون } [ المرمنون : 1 ] فما حدا مما بدأ وأن التزكية

ALUSI:91:11/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:11/r5.claim: Purification, understood as growth, is not confined to practical action and is itself an intended end, though even a prerequisite may appropriately receive emphasis.
ALUSI:91:11/r5.anchor: وأن التزكية مراداً بها الإنماء لا اختصاص لها وليست مقدمة بل مقصودة بالذات

ALUSI:91:11/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:11/r17.claim: Ṭaghwā is a verbal noun meaning transgression beyond the limit in disobedience; al-Kashshāf explains the wāw in the noun as a distinction from the adjective forms of yāʾ-root words, while al-Rāghib allows both wāw and yāʾ roots for ṭaghā.
ALUSI:91:11/r17.anchor: والطغوي مصدر من الطغيان بمعنى تجاوز الحد في العصيان

ALUSI:91:11/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r18.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI:91:11/r18.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the bāʾ as instrumental, whereas most commentators take it causally; al-Ālūsī says the difference is slight.
ALUSI:91:11/r18.anchor: والباء عند الجمهور للسببية أي فعلت التكذيب بسبب طغيانها

ALUSI:91:11/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:11/r19.claim: A further analysis makes the bāʾ attach directly to ‘denied’: Thamūd denied the torment promised by its prophet, with the punishment itself described as transgressive or excessive, like 69:5; the verbal noun intensifies without an omitted genitive.
ALUSI:91:11/r19.anchor: وجوز أن تكون صلة للتكذيب على معنى كذبت بما أوعدت به في لسان نبيها من العذاب ذي الطغوى

ALUSI:91:11/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r20.speaker: الحسن ومحمد بن كعب وحماد بن سلمة
ALUSI:91:11/r20.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, and Ḥammād ibn Salama read ṭughwāhā with ḍamma on ṭāʾ; it remains a verbal noun, compared with rujʿā and ḥusnā, and the wāw-root analysis removes the alleged irregularity.
ALUSI:91:11/r20.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ومحمد بن كعب وحماد بن سلمة طغواها بضم الطاء وهو مصدر أيضاً كالرجعى والحسنى

BAGHAWI:91:11/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:91:11/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:91:11/r1.claim: Thamud denied the truth because of their tyranny and aggression; their transgression drove them to denial.
BAGHAWI:91:11/r1.anchor: بطغيانها وعدوانها ،   أي الطغيان حملهم على التكذيب

BAYDAWI:91:11/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:91:11/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:91:11/r1.claim: Thamūd denied because of their transgression, or denied the threatened punishment called ṭaghwā, as in 69:5.
BAYDAWI:91:11/r1.anchor: بسبب طغيانها أو بما أوعدت به من عذابها ذي الطغوى كقوله تعالى فأهلكوا بالطاغية

BAYDAWI:91:11/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:91:11/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:91:11/r2.claim: The underlying form is ṭaghyā; its yāʾ became wāw to distinguish the noun from the adjective, and it is also read with ḍamma like rujʿā.
BAYDAWI:91:11/r2.anchor: وأصله طغياها وإنما قلبت ياؤه واوا تفرقة بين الأسم والصفة وقرىء بالضم كا الرجعى

BIQAI:91:11/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:11/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:11/r1.claim: The placement continues the warning signaled in Sūrat al-Balad and the preceding mention of corruption: warning is meant to urge purification, and Thamud's failure is an example for hearers.
BIQAI:91:11/r1.anchor: السياق للترهيب بما دلت عليه سورة البلد وتقديم الفجور هنا

BIQAI:91:11/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:11/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:11/r2.claim: The verb is feminine because the effect of their denial was weak: listeners readily recognize its injustice from the clarity of their sign and the ugliness of its outcome.

BIQAI:91:11/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:11/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:11/r3.claim: Thamud are singled out because their sign was exceptionally clear and especially indicative of the Hour; Quraysh and other Arabs knew them from ruins and transmitted reports.
BIQAI:91:11/r3.anchor: وخصهم لأن آيتهم مع أنها كانت أوضح الآيات في نفسها

BIQAI:91:11/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:11/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:11/r4.claim: One explanation is that their own disposition to exceed bounds—in disbelief, sins, and oppression—caused them to deny their messenger and all he brought from God.
BIQAI:91:11/r4.anchor: بسبب ما كان لنفوسهم من وصف الطغيان

BIQAI:91:11/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:11/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:11/r5.claim: Alternatively, “taghwā” refers to the threatened immediate punishment by which they were destroyed. Forms include ṭaghā/yaṭghū, yaṭghā, and ṭaghī; fatḥa makes it a noun, ḍamma a verbal noun, with wāw distinguishing the form and preferred for its strength.
BIQAI:91:11/r5.anchor: أو بما توعدوا به من العذاب العاجل وهي الطاغية

DURR:91:11/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:11/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:91:11/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says “tughwā” is the name of the punishment that came upon Thamud, so they denied their punishment.
DURR:91:11/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن عباس في قوله : { كذبت ثمود بطغواها } قال : اسم العذاب الذي جاءها

IBNASHUR:91:11/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:11/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:11/r1.claim: If the statement that the soul prospers is parenthetical, this verse answers the oath together with verse 14; the oath-response lām is omitted to shorten the long oath.
IBNASHUR:91:11/r1.anchor: لام الجواب محذوف تخفيفاً لاستطالة القسم

IBNASHUR:91:11/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:11/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:11/r2.claim: The omitted oath lām is comparable to the oath in al-Buruj, where the response follows a long series of oaths.
IBNASHUR:91:11/r2.anchor: وقد مثلوا لحذف اللام بهذه الآية

IBNASHUR:91:11/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:11/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:11/r3.claim: The passage threatens Quraysh, who knowingly defied the Messenger like Thamud; their destruction came through the swords of those they opposed, abused, and expelled.
IBNASHUR:91:11/r3.anchor: التعريض بتهديد المشركين الذين كذبوا الرسول طغياناً

IBNASHUR:91:11/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:11/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:11/r4.claim: The oath warns that Quraysh may be punished as Thamud were, because they failed to understand that Thamud's annihilation followed rejection of their messenger.

IBNASHUR:91:11/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:11/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:11/r5.claim: The object of ‘denied’ is omitted but supplied by the next verse: they denied their Messenger.
IBNASHUR:91:11/r5.anchor: محذوف لدلالة قوله بعده : { فقال لهم رسول الله }

IBNASHUR:91:11/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:11/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:11/r6.claim: The bāʾ marks cause; ṭaghwā is a verbal noun of ṭaghā, meaning excessive arrogance.
IBNASHUR:91:11/r6.anchor: وباء { بطغواها } للسببية ، أي كانت طغواها سبب تكذيبهم

IBNASHUR:91:11/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:11/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:11/r7.claim: Quraysh's rejection arose from pride that kept them from following someone they considered inferior, as their demand for a notable recipient of revelation shows.
IBNASHUR:91:11/r7.anchor: وفيه تعريض بتنظير مشركي قريش في تكذيبهم بثمود في أن سبب تكذيبهم هو الطغيان والتكبر

IBNASHUR:91:13/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:13/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:13/r5.claim: Alternatively, fāʾ gives only textual sequence, moving from a summary of Thamud's denial to its details; then ‘when their most wretched arose’ need not be treated as fronted from later.
IBNASHUR:91:13/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الفاء للترتيب الذكري المجرد وهي تفيد عطف مفصل على مجمل

IBNATIYYA:91:11/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:91:11/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:91:11/r1.claim: After mentioning the loss of one who corrupts his soul, the sūra recalls a people whose example should teach others and deter them from the same conduct.
IBNATIYYA:91:11/r1.anchor: ولما ذكر تعالى خيبة من دسى نفسه ، ذكر فرقة فعلت ذلك يعتبر بهم وينتهى عن مثل فعلهم

IBNATIYYA:91:11/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:91:11/r3.speaker: الحسن وحماد بن سليمان
IBNATIYYA:91:11/r3.claim: Al-Hasan and Hammad ibn Sulayman read ṭughwāhā with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ, a verbal noun like ʿuqbā and ruǧʿā.
IBNATIYYA:91:11/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وحماد بن سليمان «بطغواها » بضم الطاء مصدر كالعقبى والرجعى

IBNATIYYA:91:11/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:91:11/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA:91:11/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas takes ṭaghwā here as the punishment they denied until it came upon them, supported by 69:5, where Thamud are destroyed by the overwhelming blast.
IBNATIYYA:91:11/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : «الطغوى » هنا العذاب كذبوا به حتى نزل بهم ، ويؤيد هذا التأويل قوله تعالى : { فأما ثمود فأهلكوا بالطاغية }

IBNATIYYA:91:11/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:91:11/r5.speaker: جمهور المتأولين
IBNATIYYA:91:11/r5.claim: Most interpreters take the bāʾ causally: Thamud denied its prophet because of its rebellion and disbelief.
IBNATIYYA:91:11/r5.anchor: وقال جمهور المتأولين الباء سببية ، والمعنى كذبت ثمود بنبيها بسبب طغيانها وكفرها

KASHSHAF:91:11/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:11/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:11/r1.claim: The bāʾ is instrumental or causal, as in “I wrote with a pen”; ṭaghwā derives from ṭughyān, with the noun's yāʾ shifted to wāw unlike the adjective.
KASHSHAF:91:11/r1.anchor: مثلها في : كتبت بالقلم .   والطغوى من الطغيان

KASHSHAF:91:11/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:11/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:11/r2.claim: The main explanation is that Thamūd committed denial because of its transgression, as one might say someone wronged another through daring against God.
KASHSHAF:91:11/r2.anchor: مثلها في : كتبت بالقلم .   والطغوى من الطغيان

KASHSHAF:91:11/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:11/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:11/r3.claim: Alternatively, Thamūd denied the punishment threatened against it, a punishment described as overwhelming.
KASHSHAF:91:11/r3.anchor: كذبت بما أوعدت به من عذابها ذي الطغوى

KASHSHAF:91:11/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:11/r4.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF:91:11/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan read biṭughwāhā with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ, like the verbal nouns al-ḥusnā and al-rujʿā.

MAWARDI:91:11/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:11/r1.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
MAWARDI:91:11/r1.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda take the phrase to mean Thamūd's transgression and disobedience.
MAWARDI:91:11/r1.anchor: أحدها : بطغيانها ومعصيتها ،   قاله مجاهد وقتادة

MAWARDI:91:11/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:11/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب
MAWARDI:91:11/r2.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb glosses it as meaning all of Thamūd collectively.
MAWARDI:91:11/r2.anchor: الثاني : بأجمعها ،   قاله محمد بن كعب

MAWARDI:91:11/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:11/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:91:11/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes it as the punishment that came upon them; they said the punishment itself was named Ṭagwā.
MAWARDI:91:11/r3.anchor: الثالث : بعذابها ،   قاله ابن عباس . قالوا كان اسم العذاب الذي جاءها الطغوى

NASAFI:91:11/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:91:11/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:91:11/r1.claim: Ṭaghwā means their transgression; their excess was what drove them to deny the truth.
NASAFI:91:11/r1.anchor: بطغيانها إذ الحامل لهم على التكذيب طغيانهم

QURTUBI:91:11/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:11/r1.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة وغيرهما
QURTUBI:91:11/r1.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and others say طغواها means their transgression, going beyond bounds in disobedience.
QURTUBI:91:11/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : " كذبت ثمود بطغواها " أي بطغيانها ، وهو خروجها عن الحد في العصيان . قاله مجاهد وقتادة وغيرهما

QURTUBI:91:11/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:11/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:91:11/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets it as the promised punishment, called Ṭughwa because it overwhelmed them.
QURTUBI:91:11/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس " بطغواها " أي بعذابها الذي وعدت به . قال : وكان اسم العذاب الذي جاءها الطغوي ؛ لأنه طغى عليهم

QURTUBI:91:11/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:11/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب
QURTUBI:91:11/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Kab says the expression means all of it or altogether.
QURTUBI:91:11/r3.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب : " بطغواها " بأجمعها

QURTUBI:91:11/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:11/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:91:11/r4.claim: One grammatical explanation calls it a verbal noun shaped this way to match the verse endings.
QURTUBI:91:11/r4.anchor: وقيل : هو مصدر ، وخرج على هذا المخرج ، لأنه أشكل برؤوس الآي

QURTUBI:91:11/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:11/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:91:11/r5.claim: The underlying form is بطغياها; a final yāʾ in this noun pattern changes to wāw to distinguish noun from adjective.
QURTUBI:91:11/r5.anchor: وقيل : الأصل بطغياها ، إلا أن " فعلى " إذا كانت من ذوات الياء أبدلت في الاسم واوا ، ليفصل بين الاسم والوصف

QURTUBI:91:11/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:11/r6.speaker: الحسن والجحدري وحماد بن سلمة
QURTUBI:91:11/r6.claim: The general reading has fatḥa on ṭāʾ; al-Hasan, al-Jahdari, and Hammad ibn Salama use ḍamma, treating it as a verbal noun or dialect variant.
QURTUBI:91:11/r6.anchor: وقراءة العامة بفتح الطاء . وقرأ الحسن والجحدري وحماد بن سلمة ( بضم الطاء ) على أنه مصدر

RAZI:91:11/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:11/r1.speaker: الفراء
RAZI:91:11/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats ṭughyān and ṭughwā as verbal nouns, with ṭughwā chosen because it better suits the verse endings, like daʿwā from duʿāʾ.

RAZI:91:11/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:11/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:91:11/r2.claim: The well-known reading is that their transgression caused them to disbelieve, like saying someone wronged another through audacity against God.
RAZI:91:11/r2.anchor: كما تقول : ظلمني بجراءته على الله تعالى

RAZI:91:11/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:11/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:91:11/r3.claim: A second reading takes ṭughwā as their extraordinary punishment: they denied the punishment their messenger had warned them about.
RAZI:91:11/r3.anchor: أن الطغوى اسم لعذابهم الذي أهلكوا به

RAZI:91:11/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:11/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:91:11/r4.claim: The punishment reading is plausible because ṭughyān means exceeding the ordinary limit; the exceptional cry could be called ṭughwā, as in references to the calamity and overpowering punishment.
RAZI:91:11/r4.anchor: ويدل على هذا التأويل قوله تعالى : { كذبت ثمود وعاد بالقارعة }
